item.title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
item.description: Amazon-owned Bee has launched its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.

item.description: Figma is also releasing its code layers feature in open beta.

item.title: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis
item.description: The founders detailed how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process.

item.title: Gudea leverages AI to help organizations prevent social media crises before they erupt
item.description: Gudea, a company that tracks how stories and rumors spread online that describes itself as the “storm tracker for the internet,” is using AI to help organizations spot trouble brewing online before it turns into a crisis.

item.title: Flock CEO says its microphones detect ‘just gunshots’ — its website says different
item.description: Langley’s comments come amid mounting scrutiny of Flock from privacy advocates, including the ACLU, and members of the public who are concerned about the misuse of its technology.

item.title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms
item.description: The label will appear on the player page and include songs entirely generated by AI or partially, such as AI involved in composition and vocals.

item.title: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence

item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

item.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
item.description: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

item.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
item.description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.
